title: The Bremen Town Musicians
blurb: Four old animals run away together and frighten off robbers.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… on a dusty farm at the edge of a wood, there lived a Donkey who had carried sacks to the mill for many, many years.

[sad] But he was old now, and slow. And one morning he heard his master say he was not worth feeding any more.

[firmly] So the Donkey did not wait. [excited] He walked out of the gate and down the road. “I shall go to Bremen,” he said, “and be a musician!”

[curious] He had not gone far when he found a Dog lying in the road, panting.

[sad] “I am too old to hunt,” said the Dog, “and my master has no use for me.”

[warmly] “Then come with me,” said the Donkey. “I am going to Bremen to make music. You can beat the drum.”

[excited] And the Dog got up, and off they went together.

[curious] Next they passed a Cat sitting on the wall with a face like three wet weeks.

[sad] “My teeth are blunt,” said the Cat. “I would rather sit by the fire than chase mice, and nobody wants a cat like that.”

[warmly] “Come to Bremen!” said the Donkey. “You know all the night songs.”

[playfully] And then, on a gate, they found a Rooster crowing his heart out — for tomorrow he was to be the Sunday dinner. [excited] So he came too.

[softly] Now the four of them could not reach Bremen in one day, so when night came they stopped in the wood.

[curious] The Rooster flew to the top of a tree to look about… [surprised] and far off, between the branches, he saw a small yellow light.

[excited] “A house!” he called down. “There is a house!”

[whispers] They crept close and looked in at the window. [worried] And what they saw was a table covered with food… and sitting around it, a band of robbers, counting out their gold.

[thoughtful] The animals were very hungry. [mischievously] And the Donkey had an idea.

[softly] The Donkey stood at the window. The Dog climbed onto his back. The Cat climbed onto the Dog. [short pause] And the Rooster flew up and stood on top of them all.

[calmly] The Donkey counted. One… two… three.

[loudly] And they sang. The Donkey brayed, the Dog barked, the Cat yowled, the Rooster crowed — [excited] all at once, and all through the glass!

[surprised] The robbers did not stay to see what it was. They knocked over the table and ran into the dark and never came back.

[warmly] So the four old animals went in, and sat down, and ate everything on that table.

[gently] And do you know — they never did reach Bremen. They liked that little house in the wood so well that they stayed in it, all four of them, for the rest of their days.
